chapter: The House That Jazz Built and Homestead childhood
title: Her father's death and living with Aunt Jo and Paul French
summary: After her father died when she was three she stayed with Aunt Jo, reciting a poem in church.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: It wouldn't have been my uncle because he died as a youngster. And I remember going to the barber shop, everybody worked in the barber shop. In fact my grandmother had this barber shop and everybody worked in it and she had the girls work in the barber shop, too. They shaved the men and I think that's where my father met my mother, you know, working in the barber shop and they finally got married. I remember going to the barber shop

when I was 3 years old. I used to sit up on the shoe shine -- they had a shoe shine man and I used to sit up there. I remember my father when I'd come in, he'd sit me up on the stand and go through the procedure of shining my patent leather shoes. But that's just about as much as I can remember. I remember going to the funeral and in those days they had the hearses with the horse and carriages and I cried but I was crying because I wanted to be in the hearse with my mother. I guess I was with somebody else at the time.

But shortly after that I spent about two or three years living with an aunt that lived in Ranken, Pennsylvania, my mother's brother's wife in that family. And that's where I spent the early part of my childhood. I learned how to read and write and I guess I was quite a precocious kid because that's when Aunt Jo -- her name was Josephine, my uncle's name was Paul.
